item.title: Iran parliament speaker Ghalibaf in Iraq for talks
item.description: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who led negotiations with the United States to end the Middle East war, arrived in Baghdad on Wednesday for talks. Ghalibaf will head "a high-level parliamentary delegation to discuss regional developments" and "strengthen strategic cooperation between Tehran and Baghdad," Iran's Fars news agency said. The visit comes as Iraq faces pressure from Washington to disarm powerful Iran-backed armed factions, which have built considerable political and financial clout in the country. item.title: Ethiopia’s digital IDs scheme offers refugees a way out of limbo
item.description: The Ethiopian government, partnered with UNHCR, is integrating refugees via mass issuance of digital IDs. Labelled the Fayda system, Amharic for “value”, it allows refugees the freedom to move throughout the country, access to education, and to get a job. item.title: Reforestation and sustainable land & water management can help combat desertification
item.description: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Serena Ferrari, Economist and Researcher at CIRAD. Mongolia makes this particularly visible: as a pastoralist and rangeland country facing an increasingly harsh climate, it stands at the intersection of the ecological and social questions being debated at COP17. item.title: In 1993, an art historian found a forgotten painting; 33 years later, its female creator was rediscovered
item.description: A remarkable find by an art historian in 1993 ignited a relentless pursuit to recover the lost masterpieces of Michaelina Wautier. The pivotal recovery of her 'The Five Senses' series in 2020 heralded a new era, culminating in a landmark exhibition at London's Royal Academy in 2026, finally restoring her rightful legacy after centuries in the shadows.
